ToolsUptime monitor, ticket system, Dependabot, cloud billing alerts.
RisksUnpriced "unlimited" support; unpatched components; lapsing domains/certificates.
VerificationSLA metrics measured and reported; renewals tracked 60 days ahead.
DocumentationSupport log; runbooks updated after every incident (post-incident review).
Approval authorityProject Manager; client sponsor for plan changes and renewals.
Part B · Client Delivery

6. Project Structure and Repository Standards

Every project repository starts from the company template (also provided in this package as project-template/). The structure below is a real example for a Next.js + FastAPI + PostgreSQL project; adapt folder names to the chosen stack, but keep the same responsibilities. Do not create empty folders for appearance - every folder must have a purpose you can explain.

Standard project structure

web-development-project/
├── README.md
├── CHANGELOG.md
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── .gitignore
├── .env.example
├── compose.yaml
├── docs/
│   ├── requirements.md
│   ├── architecture.md
│   ├── database-design.md
│   ├── api-specification.md
│   ├── deployment.md
│   ├── security.md
│   ├── user-guide.md
│   └── adr/                 (Architecture Decision Records)
├── frontend/
│   ├── public/
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   ├── pages/  (or app/ in Next.js App Router)
│   │   ├── layouts/
│   │   ├── hooks/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   ├── styles/
│   │   └── assets/
│   └── tests/
├── backend/
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── controllers/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   ├── models/
│   │   ├── middleware/
│   │   └── config/
│   └── tests/
├── database/
│   ├── migrations/
│   └── seeds/
├── deployment/
│   ├── docker/
│   └── scripts/
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/
│   ├── CODEOWNERS
│   └── pull_request_template.md
└── qa/

What every folder and key file is for

Path Purpose Rules
README.md Front door: what the project is, prerequisites, how to run, test, deploy, who to ask A new joiner must run the app in 30 minutes using only this file
CHANGELOG.md Human-readable history of releases (Keep a Changelog format, SemVer versions) Updated in every release PR
CONTRIBUTING.md Branching, commit, PR and review rules; definition of done Mirrors this handbook
.gitignore Files Git must never track - dependencies, build output, .env, keys, IDE files, OS files Reviewed at repository creation
.env.example Names and fake/safe sample values of every environment variable Real values live only in the secret manager; update when a variable is added
compose.yaml Local development stack - app, database, mail catcher No production secrets
docs/requirements.md Discovery notes, user stories (REQ-ids), acceptance criteria, input/output register Source of truth for scope
docs/architecture.md Diagrams, stack, environments, integrations, cost estimate Updated with every architectural change
docs/database-design.md ER diagram, data dictionary, indexes, retention, backup policy Matches migrations
docs/api-specification.md Endpoints, auth, request/response, error catalogue Generated from OpenAPI where possible
docs/deployment.md Environments, CI/CD, release, rollback, DNS/TLS, monitoring, runbooks Used by DevOps and the client
docs/security.md Threat model, controls, access matrix, scan results, incident contacts Reviewed before every release
docs/user-guide.md How the client's staff operate the system Written in plain language with screenshots
docs/adr/ One short file per architecture decision Never edited after acceptance - superseded instead
frontend/public/ Static files served as-is (favicon, robots.txt, images that need stable URLs) No secrets, no private data
frontend/src/components/ Reusable UI building blocks (Button, Card, Form fields) Small, typed, accessible, tested
frontend/src/pages/ (or app/) Routes/screens One folder per route; thin - compose components
frontend/src/layouts/ Page shells (header, footer, dashboard frame)
frontend/src/hooks/ Reusable stateful logic (useDebounce, useAuth)
frontend/src/services/ API client and external calls The only place that knows URLs
frontend/src/styles/ Design tokens, global CSS Tokens mirror the Figma design system
frontend/src/assets/ Images/fonts imported by code Optimised before commit
frontend/tests/ Component and E2E tests Run in CI
backend/src/routes/ HTTP endpoints - parse, validate, call a service, return a response No business logic
backend/src/controllers/ Optional adapter between routes and services (framework dependent)
backend/src/services/ Business logic - pure, tested functions Where rules live
backend/src/models/ Database models and schemas (ORM/Pydantic) Match the migrations
backend/src/middleware/ Cross-cutting concerns - auth, request id, rate limit, error handling
backend/src/config/ Settings loaded from environment variables Fails fast when a variable is missing
backend/tests/ Unit and integration tests Use a throw-away database
database/migrations/ Versioned schema changes Never edit an applied migration
database/seeds/ Reference/demo data No real personal data
deployment/docker/ Dockerfiles, nginx config, compose overrides
deployment/scripts/ Release, backup, restore, smoke-test scripts Documented and idempotent
.github/workflows/ CI/CD pipelines Reviewed like production code
.github/CODEOWNERS Auto-requests reviewers for sensitive paths
qa/ Test plan, test cases, UAT script, reports, restore-test logs Evidence for acceptance

Naming conventions

Item Convention Example
Repositories client-project lowercase, hyphens sunrise-dental-portal
Branches type/issue-short-description feat/42-booking-form
Folders and files (frontend) Components PascalCase.tsx; others kebab-case ProductCard.tsx, use-auth.ts
Python files / functions snake_case booking_service.py, create_booking()
Python classes / TypeScript types PascalCase BookingIn, OrderStatus
Constants and env variables UPPER_SNAKE_CASE DATABASE_URL
Database tables / columns snake_case, plural tables, singular columns bookings.starts_at
API paths Lowercase plural nouns, versioned /api/v1/bookings
CSS classes Short, descriptive; BEM or utility classes consistently .card__title
Git tags vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH v1.4.0

Environment separation

Environment Purpose Data Access Deploy
Local Daily development Synthetic seeds The developer Manual (docker compose up)
Development (shared) Integration of merged work Synthetic Team Auto from develop
Staging Production-like verification, UAT Synthetic or anonymised Team + client reviewers Auto from main/release candidate
Production Real users Real Minimum named people Pipeline with manual approval

Rules: separate cloud accounts or projects per environment where possible; separate databases, secrets, API keys and payment keys (test keys outside production); staging is protected and blocked from search engines; production data is never copied to development.

# .env.example  (committed - names and SAFE sample values only)
APP_ENV=local
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://app_user:change-me-dev@localhost:5432/app_dev
JWT_SECRET=generate-a-long-random-value-per-environment
SMTP_HOST=localhost
SMTP_PORT=1025
PAYMENT_KEY_ID=test_key_id_here
PAYMENT_KEY_SECRET=test_secret_here
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000

NEVER COMMIT

Credentials, API keys, private keys (*.pem, id_ed25519), production .env files, database dumps, customer data, screenshots showing tokens, terraform.tfstate with secrets. If a secret is committed: (1) revoke and rotate it immediately, (2) tell the Technical Lead, (3) only then clean the history. Deleting the file in a new commit does not remove it from history.

Branching strategy

Branch Purpose Rules
main Always releasable; tagged for releases Protected - PR + 1 approval + passing checks; no force push
develop Integration of finished features (for multi-developer projects) Protected
feat/<id>-<name> One feature or fix Short-lived (days, not weeks); branch from develop
fix/<id>-<name> Bug fix Same as above
hotfix/<id>-<name> Urgent production fix Branch from main; merge to main and develop; tag a patch release
release/x.y.z Optional stabilisation branch for large releases

Small projects may use trunk-based flow (main + short-lived feature branches). The Technical Lead chooses at Stage 12 and records it in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Commit standards (Conventional Commits)

Format: type(scope): short imperative summary - maximum about 72 characters; body explains why.

Type Use
feat New user-visible capability
fix Bug fix
docs Documentation only
style Formatting, no logic change
refactor Code change that is neither fix nor feature
test Add or change tests
perf Performance improvement
build / ci Build system or pipeline
chore Maintenance
security Security fix (use a private channel for the details of unpatched vulnerabilities) 
feat(booking): validate slot availability on the server

Prevents double booking when two users submit at the same time.
Adds a unique constraint on (slot_id) and a regression test.
Closes #42

Pull-request procedure

  1. Branch from the latest develop/main; keep the change small (about 400 lines or fewer).
  2. Run locally - format, lint, type-check, tests. Fix everything before pushing.
  3. Open the PR using the template - what and why, how tested, screenshots, checklist; link the issue (Closes #42).
  4. CI must be green. Request a reviewer who is not the author.
  5. Reviewer applies the checklist (L5.4): correctness, tests, security, accessibility, performance, docs, no secrets.
  6. Author answers every comment; reviewer approves; squash-merge with a conventional message.
  7. Delete the branch. The merge to main triggers the pipeline to staging.

Definition of done

  • Meets every acceptance criterion in the requirement (REQ-id)
  • Unit/integration tests added and passing; critical journey covered by E2E where relevant
  • Lint and type checks pass; no new warnings
  • Reviewed and approved by another person
  • Accessibility and responsive checks done
  • No secrets, no personal data in code or logs
  • Documentation and CHANGELOG.md updated
  • Deployed to staging and smoke-tested

Versioning and releases

Use Semantic Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH - MAJOR for breaking changes, MINOR for new backward-compatible features, PATCH for fixes. Release steps: update CHANGELOG.md, tag vX.Y.Z, build once, deploy the same artefact to staging and then production, and record the deployment evidence.

Part B · Client Delivery

7. Professional Delivery Standards

These standards define what "professional" means in our deliverables. Each row has a measurable target and a way to verify it. A release is not accepted until the QA checklist (Appendix A6) shows every applicable standard as met or as a documented, client-approved exception.

7.1 Coding conventions

Standard Requirement Verified by
Language TypeScript strict for frontend/Node; Python 3.11+ with type hints for FastAPI tsc --noEmit, mypy/pyright in CI
Formatting Prettier (JS/TS/CSS/MD), Black + Ruff (Python); format on save CI format check
Linting ESLint with accessibility plugin; Ruff; zero warnings in main CI
Naming Per Section 6 table; names describe intent (calculateInvoiceTotal, not calc2) Review
Function size One responsibility; aim below about 40 lines; avoid deep nesting (more than 3 levels) Review
Comments Explain why, not what; public functions have docstrings/JSDoc Review
Dead code No commented-out code or unused exports in main Linter
Dependencies Justify each; pinned via lock file; licence recorded; no abandoned packages Dependabot, review
Secrets Read from environment variables only; the app fails fast at startup if one is missing Config tests, secret scan
Error handling Never swallow exceptions; catch where you can act Review

7.2 Reusable components

Standard Requirement
Design system Colours, type scale, spacing and radii live as design tokens (CSS variables), mirrored from Figma
Component API Typed props with sensible defaults; no hidden global state; composable (children/slots)
States Every interactive component has default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading and error states
Accessibility Built on semantic HTML; keyboard operable; labelled; documented in the catalogue
Documentation Name, purpose, props table and usage example (Storybook for larger projects)
Testing Each shared component has at least a render test and an interaction test
Reuse rule The second use of a pattern -> extract a component; the third -> it must already be one

7.3 Responsive behaviour

Standard Target
Approach Mobile-first CSS; <meta name="viewport"> on every page
Breakpoints 360 (base), 768, 1024, 1440 px - test at each; also 320 and 1920
Layout Flexbox/Grid, relative units; no horizontal scrolling at any width
Touch Tap targets at least 44x44 px; spacing between targets; no hover-only actions
Typography Body text at least 16 px; line length about 45-75 characters; fluid headings (clamp())
Images srcset/sizes, modern formats (WebP/AVIF), explicit width/height to prevent layout shift
Verification DevTools device mode + at least one real phone and one tablet

7.4 Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

Standard Requirement
Structure Landmarks (header, nav, main, footer), one h1, logical heading order, lang attribute
Keyboard Everything reachable and operable by keyboard; visible focus; no keyboard traps; skip-to-content link
Contrast Text 4.5:1 (large text 3:1); UI components and focus indicators 3:1
Alternatives Meaningful alt text; captions/transcripts for media; no information by colour alone
Forms Visible labels, error messages linked with aria-describedby, clear instructions, correct autocomplete
Motion Respect prefers-reduced-motion; no auto-playing audio; no flashing content
Verification axe/Lighthouse >= 90 with zero critical issues + manual keyboard test + one screen-reader pass

7.5 Performance

Metric (mobile, field/lab) Target ("good" thresholds per web.dev)
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) 2.5 s or less
Interaction to Next Paint (INP) 200 ms or less
Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) 0.1 or less
Lighthouse Performance (mobile) 90 or more for content sites; 80 or more for complex apps
API latency p95 under 500 ms for standard endpoints (agreed per project)
Page weight Initial JavaScript under about 200 KB gzipped for content pages; images optimised
Practices Compress and lazy-load images, subset fonts, cache static assets with long TTL + content hashing, use a CDN, avoid blocking scripts, paginate lists, add DB indexes for measured queries
Verification Lighthouse CI, WebPageTest, k6/Locust load test, DB EXPLAIN evidence

7.6 SEO (where relevant)

Standard Requirement
Rendering Content visible in HTML (SSR/SSG), not only after client JavaScript
Metadata Unique <title> and meta description per page; canonical URL; Open Graph tags
Structure Clean URLs, XML sitemap, robots.txt, correct redirects (301) for changed URLs
Content One primary topic per page; descriptive headings and link text; alt text
Structured data JSON-LD (Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, Article) validated in the Rich Results test
Technical HTTPS, mobile-friendly, fast, no broken links; submit sitemap in Search Console
Honesty No ranking guarantees - SEO results depend on competition and time

7.7 Secure authentication

Standard Requirement
Password storage Argon2id (or bcrypt) with per-user salt; never reversible encryption
Password policy Minimum 10 characters, allow long passphrases, check against breached-password lists, no forced periodic rotation without cause
Sessions/tokens httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies; access tokens 15 minutes or less; refresh rotation; logout invalidates
Brute force Rate limit and backoff per account and per IP; generic error messages
MFA Required for admin/staff accounts; offered to customers
Recovery Single-use, expiring, random reset tokens; notify the user of changes
Authorisation Server-side RBAC + ownership checks on every request; deny by default
Verification Attack tests (credential stuffing, token tampering, IDOR, CSRF, replay) pass

7.8 Database security

Standard Requirement
Network Private network only; no public database port
Access Separate least-privilege roles for application, migrations, read-only reporting
Queries Parameterised queries / ORM only - never string-built SQL
Encryption TLS in transit; encryption at rest; field-level encryption for highly sensitive data
Data minimisation Store only what is needed; define retention; pseudonymise where possible
Auditing Log privileged access and changes to sensitive tables
Backups Encrypted, off-site, restore-tested (Section 7.12)
Test data Synthetic or anonymised data only outside production

7.9 API validation

Standard Requirement
Schemas Every request validated by a typed schema (Pydantic/Zod); unknown fields rejected where relevant
Limits Maximum body size, string lengths, page sizes, upload sizes
Output Response models whitelist fields; never return password hashes or internal ids you do not need
Idempotency Idempotency-Key for payment-like POSTs; webhooks verified by signature and de-duplicated
Rate limiting Per user/IP; stricter on login, reset and expensive endpoints
CORS Allow-list of origins - never * with credentials
Contract OpenAPI is the contract; breaking changes require a new version

7.10 Error handling

Standard Requirement
Format One JSON error shape: { "error": { "code", "message", "request_id" } }
Status codes 400/422 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 429 rate limited, 5xx server
User messages Plain language, actionable, no technical details
Frontend Loading, empty and error state for every data view; retry where safe; global error boundary
Resilience Timeouts on all outbound calls; retries only for idempotent operations; graceful degradation

7.11 Logging and monitoring

Standard Requirement
Format Structured JSON with timestamp, level, message, request id, user id
Content No passwords, tokens, full card or national-ID numbers; mask personal data
Levels ERROR for action needed, WARNING for unexpected but handled, INFO for business events, DEBUG off in production
Retention Defined per project and privacy law (for example 30-90 days operational; longer for audit as agreed)
Monitoring Uptime check, error tracking, latency/error-rate dashboard, certificate expiry, disk and database alerts, backup-failure alert

7.12 Backup and recovery

Standard Requirement
Objectives RPO and RTO agreed in the SOW
Method Automated daily backups plus point-in-time recovery where the database supports it; uploaded files and configuration included
Location At least one copy outside the primary account/region; encrypted
Testing Restore test before go-live and at least quarterly, with timing recorded
Retention Documented (for example 7 daily, 4 weekly, 12 monthly)

7.13 Browser and device compatibility

Standard Requirement
Supported Latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (desktop and mobile); anything different is agreed in the SOW
Method Feature support checked on MDN/Can I use; progressive enhancement; no browser sniffing
Verification Playwright projects for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit + real-device spot checks

7.14 Documentation

Standard Requirement
Required set README, requirements, architecture, database design, API specification, deployment runbook, security notes, user guide, CHANGELOG
Quality Accurate, dated, versioned in Git, written for the next person; diagrams as source (draw.io/Mermaid)
Update rule A change is not "done" until its documentation is updated
Handover The complete pack is delivered and walked through with the client (Stage 26)
Part C · Business and People

8. Commercial Costing and Pricing

This section teaches how to cost a web project, set the selling price, and price the monthly service - and gives worked examples for small, medium and enterprise projects. The same numbers are in the Excel workbook VEL-Web-Project-Costing-Workbook.xlsx (formulas live), so you can change an assumption and see every result update.

NO VENDOR PRICES ARE STATED IN THIS HANDBOOK

Vendor prices (hosting, cloud, domains, e-mail, payment fees, licences) change often and differ by region, plan and date, and this edition could not retrieve live vendor pricing pages. Every vendor and internal-rate figure below is a clearly labelled placeholder in generic currency units (CU), shown only to demonstrate the method. Before any quotation, replace each placeholder with the figure from the vendor's official pricing page or calculator (links in 8.10), and record the region, plan, currency, date checked, usage assumptions and taxes in the Vendor Pricing Log sheet. A quotation containing an unverified price is not approved.

8.2 Formulas

Labour cost            = sum(hours x internal cost rate per role)
Subtotal               = Labour + one-time third-party costs
Contingency            = Subtotal x contingency %
Total delivery cost    = Subtotal + Contingency
Selling price          = Total delivery cost / (1 - target gross margin %)
Gross profit           = Selling price - Total delivery cost
Gross margin %         = Gross profit / Selling price
Markup %               = Gross profit / Total delivery cost        (NOT the same as margin)
Variable costs         = one-time third-party costs + commissions + bought-in contractor cost
Contribution margin    = Selling price - Variable costs            (what the project adds toward salaries and overhead)
Break-even (projects)  = Annual fixed costs / Contribution margin per project
Break-even (hours)     = hours at which gross profit reaches zero
Monthly operating cost = (vendor pass-through + service labour) x (1 + service contingency)
Annual operating cost  = Monthly operating cost x 12
Monthly service fee    = Monthly operating cost / (1 - service margin %)
MRR = sum of monthly fees      ARR = MRR x 12
Renewal fee            = max(current fee, next-year cost / (1 - service margin %))
Cost per user          = Monthly cloud cost / Active users

Margin is not markup

A 40% margin requires dividing cost by 0.60 (a 66.7% markup). Multiplying cost by 1.40 gives only a 28.6% margin. Always say which one you mean in quotes and reports.

How to set the real rate card

Internal cost per hour = (annual salary + employer costs + share of overhead) / productive hours per year (typically 70-75% of paid hours). Finance owns the rate card; developers never quote from personal rates.

Hand-calculated check - Small project

Every formula is checked by hand; compare this block with the table above.

Labour      = sum(hours x rate)           = 2,752 CU   (132 h, blended 20.85 CU/h)
Third-party = one-time licences/assets    = 40 CU
Subtotal    = 2,752 + 40                  = 2,792 CU
Contingency = 2,792 x 10.0%              = 279.2 CU
Total cost  = 2,792 + 279.2              = 3,071.2 CU
Price       = cost / (1 - 0.40)  = 3,071.2 / 0.60 = 5,118.7 -> rounded up to 5,200 CU
Gross profit= 5,200 - 3,071.2             = 2,128.8 CU
Gross margin= 2,128.8 / 5,200               = 40.9%
Markup      = 2,128.8 / 3,071.2               = 69.3%   (markup is NOT margin)
Contribution= price - (third-party + 5.0% commission) = 5,200 - 300 = 4,900 CU (94.2%)
Break-even  = fixed costs / contribution  = 360,000 / 4,900 = 73.5 small projects per year

8.6 Contribution margin and break-even

Measure Small Medium Enterprise
Variable costs (third-party + commission) 300 1,545 6,110
Contribution margin (price - variable costs) 4,900 26,355 104,090
Contribution margin % 94.2% 94.5% 94.5%
Break-even: projects per year to cover fixed costs 73.5 13.7 3.5
Blended labour cost per hour 20.85 20.55 20.58
Break-even hours (gross profit reaches zero) 222 vs 132 planned 1176 vs 700 planned 4478 vs 2870 planned

Why contribution margin looks very high here

Our developers are salaried, so their pay is a fixed cost - it is paid whether or not this project exists. Contribution margin therefore excludes labour; it shows how much each project contributes toward salaries and overhead. If the work were bought from freelancers, their cost would be variable and the contribution margin would fall to about the gross margin. The break-even figure answers: how many projects of this size per year cover our fixed costs?

Renewal pricing rule. Renew at the next-year cost plus the service margin, using the vendors' published price changes (check at renewal time) and the company's wage plan. Give the client 60 days' notice of the renewal price. Never reduce a service fee below the cost of delivering the agreed SLA. Offer a multi-year discount only if the margin stays at or above the policy minimum.

8.11 Expense classification (put it in every contract)

Type Meaning
Customer-billed cloud Client's own cloud account, paid directly to the provider (preferred)
Company-managed cloud Our account; re-billed with a stated management fee
Pass-through third party Licences and subscriptions billed at cost
Service fee Our labour and expertise

Prefer the client owning their cloud, domain and repository accounts, with us holding limited, individual access. Define additional-usage rates and caps. Avoid "unlimited" support or usage unless it is priced in.

8.12 Commercial rules

  • Quote in writing with scope, assumptions, exclusions, validity (for example 30 days), taxes, payment schedule and change-request rates.
  • Typical payment milestones: advance on SOW signature; on design approval; on staging delivery; on go-live; retention until the end of the warranty. Milestones are tied to accepted deliverables.
  • A quote includes contingency; it is not a hidden discount pool. Unused contingency is profit; overruns are managed through change control.
  • Do not discount the price without removing scope. Discount only with approval from the authorised commercial representative.
  • Estimates for fixed-price work must be reviewed by the Technical Lead; the project manager owns the budget tracking.
  • Track actual hours against the estimate weekly; report variance above 10% to the PM and TL at once.
Part C · Business and People

9. Roles, Procedures and Escalation

9.1 Roles and responsibilities

Role Core responsibilities Authority and limits How success is measured
Junior Frontend Developer Implement UI components and pages from approved designs; write component tests; fix UI bugs; follow accessibility and responsive standards; open small PRs Works from assigned tickets; no architecture changes; no production access; every PR reviewed Design match, accessibility score, review rework rate, tickets delivered vs estimate
Junior Backend Developer Implement endpoints, validation, service-layer rules and tests from the API spec; write migrations under review; fix defects No schema or auth changes without TL review; no production access; no secrets in code Test coverage of rules, defect rate, spec conformity
Full-stack Developer Deliver features end to end - UI, API, database; integrate APIs; own a module; mentor juniors Can propose design changes; merges only after review; limited staging access Feature lead time, quality at UAT, documentation completeness
UI/UX Designer Research, sitemap, wireframes, design system, hi-fi screens, prototypes, accessibility and hand-off; review the built UI Owns design decisions within the approved brief; client approves Client approval cycles, usability findings, design-implementation match
QA Engineer Test plan from requirements; manual and automated tests (Playwright, Postman); defect management; UAT support; release-readiness report Can block a release by raising a critical defect to the TL Defect escape rate, automation coverage of critical journeys
DevOps Engineer Environments, CI/CD, hosting, infrastructure as code, monitoring, backups, DNS/TLS, patching, cost alerts Production changes only through the pipeline or a documented change; least privilege Deployment success rate, mean time to restore, backup-restore test results
Technical Lead Architecture and ADRs, standards, code review of sensitive areas, security sign-off, estimation review, mentoring, go/no-go for releases Approves technical decisions and releases; escalates budget/scope to PM Quality at release, security findings, team growth, estimate accuracy
Project Manager Scope, SOW, schedule, budget, risks, change control, client communication, status reports, UAT and handover coordination Owns client relationship and plan; cannot change technical decisions alone On-time and on-budget delivery, client satisfaction, margin vs plan

Career ladder

Junior -> Developer -> Senior -> Lead. Promotion requires demonstrated gates: independent delivery, quality of reviews given, mentoring, documentation, and security awareness - not tenure alone.

9.2 Daily work procedure

Time Activity Output
Start of day Read messages; check assigned tickets and CI status; plan the day (3 priorities) Daily plan in the tracker
Stand-up (15 min) Each person: yesterday, today, blockers - no problem-solving in the meeting Blockers list with owners
Focus blocks Build, test, review - phone and notifications off Commits, PRs
Mid-day Review at least one teammate's PR; respond to review comments Review given
End of day Push work-in-progress to your branch; update tickets and timesheet; note next steps Daily log (3 lines)

Working agreements: commit at least daily; keep PRs small; never leave a branch un-pushed overnight; respond to review requests within one working day; ask early (stuck rule in Section 2).

9.3 Task assignment

Stage Rule
Ticket quality ("ready") Has a clear title, user story or problem, acceptance criteria, design/API links, estimate, priority, owner, requirement id
Assignment Technical Lead / PM assigns by skill and learning need; a junior receives work with a named reviewer
Sizing Estimate in hours or points; any ticket over 2 days is split
Work-in-progress limit Maximum 2 active tickets per person
Workflow Backlog -> Ready -> In progress -> In review -> In staging -> Accepted -> Done
Blocked Mark as blocked with the reason and owner; mention in stand-up; escalate per 9.8
Done Meets the definition of done (Section 6)

9.4 Code review (reviewer checklist)

  • Understands the purpose (ticket, requirement id); change is small and focused
  • CI green; tests added and meaningful; edge cases covered
  • Authentication and authorisation checks present on the server
  • Input validated; output encoded; SQL parameterised; no injection or XSS path
  • No secrets, tokens or personal data in code, logs, fixtures or screenshots
  • Error handling and logging consistent with standards
  • Accessibility and responsive behaviour checked (UI changes)
  • Performance: no N+1 queries, no unbounded lists, images optimised
  • Migrations safe (locks, rollback), backward compatible
  • Documentation and CHANGELOG updated
  • Comments labelled blocker, suggestion, question, nit; tone respectful

9.5 Timesheets

Rule Detail
Frequency Daily entry; weekly submission by Friday 18:00
Granularity By project and task (ticket id); 15-minute increments
Categories Billable (project work), Non-billable (training, internal, sales support), Leave
Honesty Record actual time - estimates are improved only by accurate actuals
Approval PM approves weekly; discrepancies above 10% against the plan are explained
Use Invoicing (time-and-materials), margin tracking, estimate calibration. Never used to measure keystrokes or punish honest reporting

9.6 Leave and handover

Before leave of more than one day, complete and share a handover note with your mentor/TL:

HANDOVER NOTE
Name / dates away:
Project / tickets in progress (links, state, next step):
Branches and PRs open (links, review state):
Environments touched (what is deployed where, anything fragile):
Pending client communication / deadlines:
Where the notes and credentials access are (never the credentials themselves):
Who to contact for what while I am away:
Known risks:

Rules: push all work; no one should need your laptop; production access is never given to "cover" a colleague - the TL arranges authorised cover.

9.7 Documentation rules

  • Documentation lives in the repository (docs/) and in the shared knowledge base; no knowledge only in chat or in one person's head.
  • Every module owner updates docs in the same PR as the code.
  • Decisions are recorded as ADRs; incidents as post-incident reviews; meetings as short minutes with action owners.
  • Diagrams are stored as editable source files.

9.8 Escalation

Severity Definition Example Initial response (internal target - set per SLA) Escalate to
P1 Critical Production down, data loss or security breach Site returns 500 for all users; leaked credentials Immediately; page the on-call and TL TL + PM at once; Director and client sponsor within 1 hour
P2 High Major feature broken, no workaround Payments failing for some users Within 1 hour TL, PM
P3 Medium Feature degraded, workaround exists Search slow Same working day Mentor / TL
P4 Low Cosmetic or request Typo, minor layout issue Within 2 working days Ticket owner

How to escalate: state what happened, impact, since when, what you tried, what you need. Do not wait for certainty. Keep a timeline of actions during incidents.

SECURITY INCIDENTS

If you suspect a leaked secret, a compromised account or a data breach: (1) stop - do not delete evidence, (2) tell the TL within one hour, (3) revoke/rotate exposed credentials with the TL's direction, (4) the PM and Director decide client and legal notifications. Never discuss an incident in public channels or social media.

9.9 Communication and conduct

  • Client communication goes through the PM or the agreed channel; developers do not agree to scope or price changes in chat.
  • Write short, specific messages; summarise decisions in the ticket; confirm agreements in writing.
  • Be honest about status and risk - bad news early is cheaper than bad news late.
  • Respect confidentiality: no client details on public forums, AI tools or personal accounts without approval.
  • Credit sources; never present copied code or text as your own; respect open-source licences.
Part D · Practice and Sources

10. Practical Employee Projects and Certification

Seven practical projects take the trainee from a single page to a complete simulated client engagement. Each project has a brief, acceptance criteria, skills practised, deliverables and a reviewer. Projects are built in the training organisation on GitHub, follow the repository standards (Section 6) and are accepted only after code review and demonstration.

# Project Level Duration Reviewer
1 Responsive business website 2 1 week Mentor
2 Multi-page corporate website 2 2 weeks Mentor + UX
3 Authentication-enabled web application 3 2 weeks Technical Lead
4 CRUD application with database 3-4 2 weeks Technical Lead
5 E-commerce prototype 5 2 weeks Technical Lead
6 SaaS admin dashboard 5 2 weeks Technical Lead + QA
7 Complete simulated client project 1-5 3 weeks PM + Technical Lead + QA

Project 1 - Responsive business website

Item Detail
Brief A 3-5 section one-page site for a fictional local business (clinic, bakery, gym) with hero, services, about, contact form and footer
Stack HTML5, CSS3 (Flexbox/Grid), a little JavaScript
Must include Semantic structure; mobile-first responsive layout; accessible navigation and form; optimised images; SEO metadata; Lighthouse >= 90 (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO)
Deliverables GitHub repo with README, deployed page on free static hosting, Lighthouse report
Acceptance Passes W3C validator; works at 360/768/1024/1440 px; keyboard-only usable; no console errors

Project 2 - Multi-page corporate website

Item Detail
Brief A 6-8 page corporate site (Home, About, Services, Service detail, Blog/News, Contact) with a design from the UX Designer
Stack Next.js + TypeScript; content in Markdown/MDX or a headless CMS
Must include Shared layout and component library; SEO (metadata, sitemap, robots.txt, structured data); image optimisation; a working contact form with server-side validation and e-mail; 404 page
Deliverables Repo with docs, Storybook or component catalogue, Playwright smoke test, deployed preview, performance report
Acceptance Matches the design within tolerance; LCP <= 2.5 s on mobile profile; accessibility checklist passed

Project 3 - Authentication-enabled web application

Item Detail
Brief A member area - register, verify e-mail, log in, log out, reset password, profile, roles (member/admin)
Stack Next.js + FastAPI (or Node) + PostgreSQL
Must include Argon2id hashing; httpOnly cookies or short-lived JWT + refresh; rate limiting; RBAC with ownership checks; validation; error format; request ids; tests for the access matrix
Deliverables Repo, API specification, security notes (docs/security.md), test report
Acceptance Technical Lead's five attack tests fail (credential stuffing, token tampering, IDOR, CSRF, brute force); no secrets in Git history

Project 4 - CRUD application with a database

Item Detail
Brief A bookings or inventory app with at least six related tables - list, search, filter, paginate, create, edit, delete, export CSV, upload a document
Stack Next.js + API + PostgreSQL + migrations
Must include ER diagram and data dictionary; migrations and seeds; indexes backed by EXPLAIN; transactions for multi-step operations; file upload hardening; Docker Compose; CI pipeline; backup and restore drill
Deliverables Repo, docs/database-design.md, restore-test log, CI run
Acceptance Fresh clone runs with one command; migrations build an identical schema; concurrency test passes; restore completes within the stated RTO

Project 5 - E-commerce prototype

Item Detail
Brief Catalogue, product page, cart, checkout, order history, admin product management; payment in sandbox/test mode only
Stack Next.js + API + PostgreSQL + payment provider sandbox
Must include Server-side price and total calculation; tax and discount rules with unit tests; order state machine; webhook verification and idempotency; order e-mails; inventory handling with transactions
Deliverables Repo, API spec, payment flow diagram, test matrix (success, decline, duplicate webhook, refund)
Acceptance No price or total can be changed from the browser; duplicate webhooks do not double-process; Playwright test completes a purchase

Project 6 - SaaS admin dashboard

Item Detail
Brief A multi-tenant dashboard - organisations, users and roles, invitations, subscription plan display, usage charts, audit log
Stack Next.js + API + PostgreSQL; a charts library
Must include Tenant isolation on every query; role-based UI and API; audit trail; responsive data tables with server pagination; accessibility for tables and charts; monitoring and logging; CI/CD to staging
Deliverables Repo, architecture doc with tenant model, security tests for cross-tenant access, dashboards for logs/uptime
Acceptance A user from tenant A can never read tenant B data (tests prove it); p95 API latency within target under a load test

Project 7 - Complete simulated client project

The capstone runs the full 27-stage lifecycle with a trainer acting as the client.

Item Detail
Brief The trainer supplies a one-paragraph enquiry for a realistic client (for example a dental clinic wanting a website with online booking and payment)
Team 3-4 trainees in roles (PM, UX, full-stack, QA/DevOps); roles rotate within the capstone
Required artefacts Qualified-lead sheet, questionnaire answers, requirements, competitor matrix, costed SOW, feature-freeze register, sitemap, Figma design, architecture + ADRs, DB design, repository, working application, test report, security report, staging deployment, UAT sign-off, production-like deployment with domain and HTTPS, handover pack, monitoring and a first monthly report
Assessment Trainer-client acceptance; Technical Lead code and security review; PM review of documents and costing; 30-minute oral defence by each trainee
Pass mark Every gate evidenced; no critical security finding; costing reconciles; the client can operate the system from the handover pack

CERTIFICATION

On passing Project 7 and all level gates, the Technical Lead and Director issue the Delivery Readiness Certificate. The employee may then join supervised client projects. Certification is reviewed annually.

Project rubric (used by reviewers)

Dimension Weight Excellent means
Functionality 20% All acceptance criteria met; edge cases handled
Code quality 20% Clean, typed, tested, small PRs, consistent standards
Security 20% Controls implemented and verified; no secrets; attack tests pass
UX and accessibility 15% Responsive, accessible, polished states
Engineering practice 15% Git history, CI, review, Docker, docs
Documentation and communication 10% Clear README, ADRs, honest status, good demo

A project is accepted at 70% overall with no dimension below 50% and no failure in Security.

Reading plan by level

Level Read first Then
1 MDN "Learn web development" and HTTP overview; web.dev "Learn Responsive Design" OWASP Top 10 introduction
2 MDN HTML, CSS, JavaScript guides; HTML Living Standard (reference); web.dev Accessibility and Performance paths TypeScript handbook; react.dev/learn (complete the tutorial); Next.js "Learn" course
3 FastAPI tutorial (all sections: query, body, dependencies, security, testing) or Django tutorial; Node.js docs OWASP API Security Top 10, Authentication and Session cheat sheets
4 PostgreSQL tutorial, SQL commands, indexes, transactions, backup EXPLAIN guide; migrations tool docs
5 Pro Git ch. 1-3, 7; GitHub Actions docs; Docker "Get started" Playwright intro; cloud provider "getting started"; OWASP ASVS

How to read documentation

1) Read the overview and concepts page. 2) Run the smallest example. 3) Change one thing and observe. 4) Read the reference for the exact option you used. 5) Write three lines of notes with the link in your training repository. Always note the version you used.

Reliability rules for sources

  • Prefer the official site; check the "last updated" date and the version selector.
  • For anything involving prices, limits, licences, security advisories or compliance, use only the official page dated within the last 30 days.
  • Do not rely on AI-generated answers, forums or videos as evidence for a client decision - verify against official documentation or run a test.
  • Record source links in ADRs and in docs/architecture.md.

Part E · Toolkit

A9. Project Costing Spreadsheet Specification

This is the specification for the Project Costing Workbook. A working implementation is supplied as VEL-Web-Project-Costing-Workbook.xlsx (built to this specification, with live formulas). Use the workbook for every quotation; keep one copy per client version in the project folder.

1. Principles

  • Inputs are blue cells; formulas are black. Inputs live only on Assumptions, Estimate hours, Operating vendor lines and VendorLog.
  • No vendor price is typed without a VendorLog row (source URL, date checked, region, currency, plan, assumptions, checked-by).
  • Currency is stated once on Assumptions; all other sheets inherit it. Taxes are excluded from every figure and added in the quotation.
  • Margin and markup are separate, labelled outputs. Prices round up to the configured step.
  • The workbook is read-only for finished quotes (save as PDF + archive); changes create a new version number.

2. Sheet specification

Sheet Purpose Key contents
README Instructions, colour legend, warnings, version Placeholder warning; how to use; change log
Assumptions Global inputs Currency; rate card (role, cost/hour); contingency % per size; target margin % per size; commission %; annual fixed costs; price rounding; service contingency and margin; renewal inflation (vendor, wages)
Estimate Project cost and price Work items x role x hours (Small/Medium/Enterprise), cost per line, labour subtotal, third-party one-time, subtotal, contingency, total cost, selling price, gross profit, gross margin %, markup %, variable cost, contribution margin, break-even projects, break-even hours
Operating Recurring cost and service price Vendor pass-through lines, service labour (hours x rate), service contingency, monthly operating cost, annual operating cost, monthly fee, MRR, ARR, service margin, renewal fee
Scenarios Usage-based cost at 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 / 100,000 users Compute, database, storage, network, monitoring (inputs from calculator), total, cost per user, margin check
VendorLog Evidence for every external price Vendor, item, plan, region, currency, unit price, quantity assumption, URL, date checked, checked by, reviewer
Summary One-page result for the quotation Price, GM %, CM, break-even, monthly fee, annual fee, renewal

3. Formulas (Excel notation)

Output Formula
Line cost =Hours * VLOOKUP(Role, RateCard, 2, FALSE)
Labour =SUM(line costs)
Subtotal =Labour + ThirdPartyOneTime
Contingency =Subtotal * ContingencyPct
Total delivery cost =Subtotal + Contingency
Selling price =CEILING(TotalCost / (1 - TargetMargin), RoundTo)
Gross profit =Price - TotalCost
Gross margin % =GrossProfit / Price
Markup % =GrossProfit / TotalCost
Variable cost =ThirdPartyOneTime + Commission * Price
Contribution margin =Price - VariableCost
Break-even projects / year =AnnualFixed / ContributionMargin
Blended rate =Labour / TotalHours
Break-even hours =(Price - ThirdParty - Contingency - Commission*Price) / BlendedRate
Monthly operating cost =(VendorTotal + ServiceLabour) * (1 + ServiceContingency)
Annual operating cost =MonthlyCost * 12
Monthly service fee =CEILING(MonthlyCost / (1 - ServiceMargin), 5)
MRR / ARR =SUM(monthly fees) / =MRR * 12
Next-year cost =(VendorTotal*(1+VendorInflation) + ServiceLabour*(1+WageInflation)) * (1 + ServiceContingency)
Renewal fee / month =MAX(CurrentFee, CEILING(NextYearCost / (1 - ServiceMargin), 5))
Cost per active user =TotalMonthlyCost / ActiveUsers

4. Validation and controls

Control Rule
Data validation Margins and contingency between 0 and 0.9; hours >= 0; role chosen from the rate card list
Conditional formatting Gross margin below policy minimum -> red; vendor price older than 30 days -> amber; missing VendorLog URL -> red
Protection Formula cells locked; inputs unlocked
Cross-check Summary totals equal the sum of detail sheets (a check cell shows OK/ERROR)
Review Technical Lead reviews hours; PM reviews commercial terms; a second person re-opens at least 20% of vendor links
Versioning File name client-project-costing-vN.xlsx; changes logged in README

5. Quotation output checklist

  • Scope and assumptions match the SOW
  • Every vendor price traces to a VendorLog row dated within 30 days
  • Contingency included; margin stated as margin, not markup
  • Taxes excluded and stated; currency stated
  • Monthly service fee, annual fee and renewal rule included
  • Break-even and gross-margin check passed policy minimum
  • Reviewed by Technical Lead and PM; approved by the authorised commercial representative

A10. Glossary

Term Meaning
A record / AAAA DNS record mapping a name to an IPv4 / IPv6 address
ADR Architecture Decision Record - short document capturing a technical decision and its reasons
API Application Programming Interface - a defined way for programs to talk to each other
ARIA Accessible Rich Internet Applications - attributes that add accessibility meaning when HTML alone is not enough
ARR / MRR Annual / Monthly Recurring Revenue
Argon2id A modern, slow, memory-hard password-hashing algorithm
Authentication / Authorisation Proving who you are / deciding what you may do
Backup / restore A copy of data / the act of bringing it back; only a tested restore proves a backup
Branch An independent line of development in Git
CDN Content Delivery Network - caches content close to users
CI / CD Continuous Integration (build and test every change) / Continuous Delivery or Deployment
CMS Content Management System
Contingency Reserve added to an estimate for uncertainty
Contribution margin Price minus variable costs - what a project adds toward fixed costs and profit
CORS Cross-Origin Resource Sharing - browser rule controlling which sites may call an API
CRUD Create, Read, Update, Delete
CSP Content Security Policy - header that restricts what a page may load or run
CSRF Cross-Site Request Forgery - tricking a browser into sending an unwanted request
DNS Domain Name System - turns names into IP addresses
Docker / container Tool and format for packaging an app with its dependencies so it runs the same everywhere
ER diagram Entity-Relationship diagram of database tables and relations
Gate A mandatory approval point; work does not continue until it is signed
Gross margin (Price - direct cost) / price
HSTS HTTP Strict Transport Security - tells browsers to use only HTTPS
HTTP / HTTPS The web protocol / HTTP over TLS encryption
IaC Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/OpenTofu)
Idempotent Repeating the operation has the same effect as doing it once
IDOR Insecure Direct Object Reference - reading another user's record by changing an id
INP / LCP / CLS Core Web Vitals - interaction responsiveness, loading speed, visual stability
JWT JSON Web Token - signed token carrying claims
Markup (Price - cost) / cost; not the same as margin
Migration Versioned script that changes the database schema
MFA Multi-Factor Authentication
OWASP Open Worldwide Application Security Project - security standards and guidance
PR Pull Request - a proposed change reviewed before merging
RBAC Role-Based Access Control
REST Architectural style for APIs using resources and HTTP methods
RPO / RTO Recovery Point Objective (acceptable data loss) / Recovery Time Objective (acceptable downtime)
SEO Search Engine Optimisation
SLA / SLO Service Level Agreement / Objective - agreed service targets
SOW Statement of Work - the agreed scope, price and terms
SQL injection Attack that inserts SQL through unvalidated input; prevented by parameterised queries
SSR / SSG Server-Side Rendering / Static Site Generation
TLS Transport Layer Security - encryption used by HTTPS
UAT User Acceptance Testing - the client verifies the product against acceptance criteria
WCAG Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (target: 2.2 level AA)
XSS Cross-Site Scripting - injecting script into a page viewed by other users
